subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix disruptive scroll jumps primarily in the pi-tui renderer, in OpenClaw-owned viewport/follow state, or through an explicit TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the permanent fix is a terminal UX and dependency-ownership decision rather than a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Fix renderer and anchoring
options.body: Prefer a live-proven renderer or TUI anchoring fix that stops content-driven full redraws from clearing/jumping scrollback while preserving normal tail-follow behavior.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose a terminal preference if maintainers want user control, accepting the extra settings surface and fresh/upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Wait for upstream pi-tui
options.body: Keep this open until upstream renderer behavior is fixed and OpenClaw can safely bump or patch the dependency with PTY proof.

recommendation.title: Fix renderer and anchoring
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven renderer or TUI anchoring fix that stops content-driven full redraws from clearing/jumping scrollback while preserving normal tail-follow behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent merged history in the TUI state and ChatLog/session behavior touched by this issue.
